content: The Department of Health Policy and Administration (HPAA) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is one of eight departments within the School of Public Health. It is one of the oldest health management programs in the United States and is dedicated to training future leaders in public health and health administration. The department offers undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral programs, as well as one-year certificate programs in disaster management and healthcare quality. The master’s program includes online options for the Master of Health Administration (MHA) and Master of Public Health (MPH). Recently, the department received approval to offer a master’s degree in disaster management, one of the few such programs in the country. The department was established on June 7, 1940, as one of the first four departments in the School of Public Health, which was the first public school of public health in the United States. Initially part of the School of Medicine, the department was led by Milton J. Rosenau, a prominent public health figure. In the 1960s, the department expanded its faculty to include experts in public administration, sociology, healthcare finance, and healthcare administration, reflecting the growing demand for health administrators following the introduction of medical care legislation. In 1969, the department launched the Off-Campus Master’s Program, the first public health program in the U.S. to offer courses outside the main campus. This program began in Raleigh and later expanded to Asheville and Fayetteville. Over the years, the department introduced a baccalaureate degree in 1972, a PhD program in 1982, and a Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) program in 2005, which was the first DrPH program in the U.S. to be offered via distance learning. The department’s academic offerings include undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral degrees, as well as certificate programs in disaster management and patient safety. The curriculum is designed to equip future health leaders with the skills and knowledge needed to manage healthcare organizations effectively. Coursework includes financial management, health law, epidemiology, environmental health, and health behavior. The Bachelor of Science in Public Health (BSPH) program prepares students for careers in various healthcare settings, including hospitals, public health organizations, and health insurance companies. It also provides a foundation for graduate studies in fields such as public health, law, medicine, and business administration. Students begin the program in their junior year and complete an internship between their junior and senior years to gain practical experience and clarify career goals. The Residential Master’s Program offers three degrees: MPH, MHA, and Master of Science in Public Health (MSPH). The MPH is designed for students with doctoral-level professional degrees, while the MSPH focuses on health policy analysis and advocacy. The MHA prepares students for management roles in healthcare organizations. The program is campus-based, with students completing a full course load over two years. MHA and MSPH students must complete 61 credit hours and a 12-week internship, while MPH students complete 42 credit hours and a 6-week internship. The Executive Master’s Program (EMP) is tailored for working professionals who wish to pursue an advanced degree while maintaining their current employment. It offers online MHA and MPH tracks, with the MHA focusing on healthcare management and the MPH on public health leadership. The program combines online coursework with three on-campus sessions totaling 24 days. Each cohort admits 40 students, with two cohorts starting annually in December and August. Admission requirements include a GRE score in the 50th percentile and at least three years of healthcare experience. The Master of Science in Disaster Management (MSDM) program is designed for professionals in disaster-related fields, such as emergency management, law enforcement, and public health. The 60-credit-hour curriculum covers topics such as disaster science, public decision-making, and disaster management systems. The program is primarily online and is expected to enroll 35 students annually. The PhD program in Health Policy and Administration prepares students for careers in health services and health policy research. The curriculum includes courses in research design, quantitative methods, and health policy. Students develop expertise in a specific area through a minor, which can be disciplinary (e.g., economics, epidemiology) or interdisciplinary (e.g., decision sciences, quality and access). The program also offers a collaborative PhD with the School of Pharmacy, focusing on pharmacoeconomics and pharmaceutical outcomes research. The Doctoral Program in Health Leadership (DrPH) is a unique distance-learning program designed for mid-level healthcare professionals aiming to become top leaders. The program combines online coursework with three on-campus sessions per year. Students focus on their dissertation in the third year and can take up to two electives. The program requires approximately 16 hours of work per week and is designed to accommodate full-time professionals. The Community Preparedness and Disaster Management Certificate Program provides training for community leaders and emergency management personnel. The one-year online program includes four courses, three of which can be transferred to a graduate degree program. Topics include disaster management systems, forensic epidemiology, and risk assessment. The Healthcare Quality and Patient Safety Certificate Program is a one-year online program for professionals working to improve healthcare quality. It includes four courses, three of which can be transferred to a graduate degree program. The curriculum covers quality of care data analysis, quality improvement strategies, and cost-effectiveness of quality programs. The department’s faculty have received numerous awards for their contributions to health services research and education. Notable achievements include the John D. Thompson Prize for Young Investigators, the Distinguished Service Award from the American Association of Public Health Dentistry, and the Vision Award for Groundbreaking Research in Chronic Illness Care. The department has been led by several distinguished chairs, including John J. Wright, M.D., and Peggy Leatt, Ph.D., who currently serves as chair. It is ranked 3 among health administration programs and its Executive Master’s Program is ranked 1 for physician-executives by Modern Healthcare. The School of Public Health is also highly ranked, tied with Harvard University as the leading public school of public health.
